thread.title: Grants awarded to support arts programs for military communities across New Mexico
thread.title_full: Grants awarded to support arts programs for military communities across New Mexico

author: New Mexico Sun
title: Grants awarded to support arts programs for military communities across New Mexico
text:
Ten organizations across New Mexico have been awarded grants to support arts programming for military personnel, veterans, and their families. Each group will receive $2,500 through the New Mexico Arts & The Military Mini Grant Program, which is aimed at providing either art programs or capacity building projects that serve active-duty and veteran audiences.
The grant recipients include Artrageous Artreach, CENTER, Groove ArtSpace, National Ghost Ranch Foundation, Northwest New Mexico Arts Council, Off Center Community Arts Project, Otero Arts, SouthWest Writers, PopUp Show, and New Mexico Veterans Integration Center. These organizations are located throughout Bernalillo, Otero, Rio Arriba, San Juan, Santa Fe, and Valencia Counties.
Michelle Laflamme-Childs, Executive Director of New Mexico Arts, said: "The Arts & The Military Mini Grants program expands arts engagement opportunities, enhances well-being, and elevates quality of life. New Mexico Arts is honored to cultivate partnerships with organizations serving the state’s military community."
Funded projects for 2026 include a range of activities such as photography mentorships with exhibitions, writing workshops held statewide, participatory music performances in VFW halls, art instructional classes, and an intensive therapeutic arts retreat. SouthWest Writers will continue its work by offering public reading venues for writers featured in its anthologies Holes in Our Hearts and Unbreaking the Circle.
Jim Tritten, Military Grants Program Manager for SouthWest Writers stated: "Authors who published in the two previous anthologies benefited from public readings. This both supported the healing process and gave the participants new insights into how their stories affect individuals who have never been exposed to military life."
This year’s grant cycle introduces a Peer Learning Community component to facilitate networking and sharing best practices among grantees. According to New Mexico Arts (NMA), this initiative aims to empower organizations that address the needs of veterans and active-duty service members along with their families.
New Mexico is home to about 141,750 veterans living across all counties. More than 21,800 active-duty service members—including those in the National Guard—are stationed at five bases statewide. These personnel are joined by roughly 7,600 adult spouses and 12,500 children living in New Mexico.
New Mexico Arts operates as the state’s official arts agency under the Department of Cultural Affairs. It manages programs such as One Percent for Public Art and provides funding as well as technical assistance to nonprofit groups supporting community arts efforts across New Mexico. Additional information can be found at www.nmarts.org.
